subject: brain
topic: Your brain fills in what your eyes do not see
angle: People often fail to notice large changes in their immediate environment due to a lack of attention or encoding time, even when those changes have consequences for their actions.
title: The World You Do Not See

hooks.text: What did you miss in the last hour?
Your eyes see it. Your brain ignores it.
You are moving through a world you do not see.
A chair moves in an empty room.
Your brain fills in the gaps.

reveal.headline: You do not notice large changes in your visual field.
reveal.body: People often fail to notice significant changes in visual scenes, even when those changes happen right in front of their eyes.

explain.headline: Your brain lacks the time to encode every object.
explain.body: A major cause of change blindness is a lack of encoding time or attention to each object in your immediate environment.

matters.headline: The world moves without your consent.
matters.body: That may be why you miss significant shifts in your surroundings. Your brain fills in the gaps, letting large changes go undetected.

example.headline: A new chair in a busy office.
example.body: You walk into a room where a piece of furniture has been moved. You see the room, but you do not see the change. Your brain treats the space as it was before. It assumes the environment is stable. You do not register the shift because your attention is elsewhere. You move through the day based on a mental map that is slightly out of date. The physical world is changing, but your perception remains fixed on the past version of the room.

verdict: The evidence confirms that people frequently fail to notice significant changes in scenes, though these failures can be mitigated by increased attention or saliency.
caveat: The research identifies various factors like encoding time, saliency, and the speed of change as critical variables that influence whether a change is actually perceived.
caption:
Your brain often fails to register significant changes in your immediate surroundings.

Research shows that change blindness occurs because of a lack of encoding time or attention. These perceptions can be influenced by the saliency of an object and the speed of the change.

What is one thing in your home that has changed recently without you noticing?
